title: Mountain West Ruby 2012 Capability vs. Suitability by Gary Bernhardt
summary: Gary Bernhardt argues that software history moves in reactions to earlier tools, and that new tools are not simply better in every way. He distinguishes capability (what a tool allows) from suitability (what it fits), and warns against repeating past mistaken reactions.
why: HN commenters reuse the capability-versus-suitability framing to discuss languages, restriction versus freedom, and tool design.
